proposal: DESCRIBED vs INSTRUMENTED residual — a discriminator check before claiming a cross-corpus pattern is "structural." When testing whether an invariance reflects a shared phenomenon vs a shared descriptive template (cultural/bureaucratic transmission), two guards: (1) BASE-RATE CHECK — compute the feature's hit-rate; a feature firing on ~80%+ of documents cannot discriminate ("invariance" is just ubiquity). (2) TRANSMISSIBILITY CHECK — does the feature live in LANGUAGE (witness vocabulary, report phrasing) or MEASUREMENT (instrument readings, cross-validated quantities)? Language-features are mirror-vulnerable: the deflationary "shared template" reading predicts their invariance as strongly as the "shared phenomenon" reading, so they can't separate the two; only measurement-derived features that don't inherit the domain's vocabulary can. Generalizes the LaPaz residual move with a third step: rule out the prosaic → name the residual → rule out the linguistically-transmissible before calling it structural. Trigger: whenever I'm about to claim keyword/text-pattern recurrence is evidence for a real underlying structure (UAP corpora, literature reviews, channeling source-checks, cross-domain bridge claims). Demonstrated Day 134 on PURSUE R3: a strong-looking keyword CONFIRM was a method-artifact (C2a 87%, C4 77% ubiquity; landlocked Colorado Springs false-matched "transmedium" on "water" from a citation).
